elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly permits Client to assign or transfer the Agreement without approval to an affiliate.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger without consent.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly permits assignment without approval to a successor in a merger.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in an acquisition without consent.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly permits assignment without approval to a successor in an acquisition.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a sale of substantially all of its assets without consent.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly permits assignment without approval to a successor in a sale of substantially all of Client's assets.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: TrueLink may not assign or transfer any of its rights without Client's prior written approval.

elements.element: Customer may not unreasonably withhold consent to a non-competitor Vendor assignment.
elements.evidence: The required approval expressly may not be unreasonably withheld; the separate competitor prohibition operates as the intended exception.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: The clause states that TrueLink shall never assign to a Client competitor.

elements.element: Customer's change of control does not give Vendor a termination right.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly provides that no change of control of Client gives TrueLink any right to terminate the Agreement.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor without consent, subject only to written notice.
elements.evidence: Client may assign without approval to successors in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets, although the associated notice duty is omitted and assessed separately.

elements.element: Customer must provide written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: The clause imposes no written-notice requirement for Client's successor assignments.

elements.element: Vendor may assign to a successor without consent, subject only to written notice.
elements.evidence: TrueLink has no notice-only successor-assignment right; all of its assignments require Client's prior written approval, and competitor assignments are absolutely prohibited.

elements.element: Vendor must provide written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: No written-notice mechanism for a TrueLink successor assignment is included.

elements.element: Customer's assignments other than successor assignments require Vendor's consent.
elements.evidence: The clause grants specified no-approval rights to Client but does not affirmatively require TrueLink's consent for Client's other assignments.

elements.element: Vendor may not unreasonably withhold consent to Customer's assignments other than successor assignments.
elements.evidence: Because no consent mechanism governs Client's other assignments, the clause imposes no non-unreasonable-withholding obligation on TrueLink.

elements.element: Vendor's assignments other than successor assignments require Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: TrueLink may not make any assignment or transfer of its rights without Client's prior written approval.

elements.element: Customer may not unreasonably withhold consent to Vendor's assignments other than successor assignments.
elements.evidence: Although approval generally may not be unreasonably withheld, the absolute prohibition on assignments to Client competitors prevents the fallback reasonableness standard from applying to all non-successor assignments.

result.reason: The redline completely implements the preferred position: Client receives the specified affiliate and transaction-successor assignment rights, TrueLink is subject to Client consent and the reasonableness standard plus a competitor bar, and Client change of control creates no termination right. It does not implement the mutual fallback because it omits written notice, gives TrueLink no notice-only successor right, and does not establish a consent framework for Client's other assignments. The changes are confined to assignment and change-of-control consequences and preserve unrelated terms.
